summary: This House resolution honors the victims and survivors of the August 27, 2025 mass shooting at Annunciation Catholic Church and School in Minneapolis by condemning the attack, offering condolences to families, commending first responders and caregivers, and expressing solidarity with the affected community and other faith institutions.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely commemorative and contains no provisions, authorizations, or references related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets.
No language in the bill addresses tax policy, rates, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
While the text commends medical caregivers, it does not engage with healthcare policy, coverage systems, or regulatory frameworks.
The resolution condemns a mass shooting but proposes no regulatory changes, restrictions, or protections concerning firearms.
The bill has no connection to immigration policy, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions or references relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The text contains nothing about military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental regulations, climate measures, or conservation policies are mentioned.
The resolution does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policies.
Although the shooting occurred at a school, the bill offers no policy changes regarding education funding, standards, or school choice.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-related legislation appear in the text.
The bill condemns violence and praises law enforcement but introduces no sentencing reforms, policing changes, or justice-system policies.
The resolution has zero connection to trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization issues.
No fiscal policy, deficit, or debt-reduction measures are discussed.
The bill contains no language concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
Foreign assistance or international aid is not mentioned.
No provisions relate to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
The text does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, union, or workplace-policy content is present.

The resolution expresses solidarity with faith communities and notes the attack on a place of worship, but it does not advance or alter any legal framework regarding religious exemptions versus anti-discrimination protections.
